planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring once soil is workable so roots establish before summer heat.

directions: Rose Quick Fire is a sport of the popular Quick Fire hydrangea that opens its conical white panicles noticeably earlier in summer than most panicle hydrangea cultivars. The florets quickly blush a clear rose-pink, giving a two-toned white-and-pink display for weeks before the whole panicle deepens to a richer rose shade by late summer. Sturdy, upright stems hold the flower heads well without staking. It blooms on new wood, so it can be pruned hard each late winter to control size and encourage strong flowering stems.

planting.note: Set out in spring so the shrub can establish roots before its first full flowering season.

directions: Burgundy Lace bears relatively open, airy flower panicles that begin creamy white and gradually take on a distinctive wine-red to burgundy flush as the blooms age through late summer, a deeper color shift than most white panicle hydrangea cultivars show. The looser, lacier flower structure gives the shrub a softer texture than dense mophead types. It grows into a large, multi-stemmed shrub and flowers reliably on new wood, so it tolerates hard renewal pruning in late winter.

planting.note: Install in spring in average, well-drained soil to allow full establishment before winter.

directions: White Moth is an older panicle hydrangea selection valued for its loose, lacecap-like flower trusses of pure white florets, a more delicate and open look than the dense conical panicles typical of most paniculata cultivars. Flowering runs from mid- to late summer on a vigorous, upright multi-stemmed shrub. It has long been grown in collector and botanical garden settings rather than mass retail, but performs with the same easy culture as other panicle hydrangeas, tolerating full sun and a hard late-winter pruning.
sources: Chicago Botanic Garden Plant Evaluation Notes

planting.note: Plant in spring where its narrow upright form can be used as a vertical accent or screen.

directions: Greenspire stands out among panicle hydrangea cultivars for its narrow, upright, almost columnar growth habit, making it useful as a vertical accent or screening plant where a typical wide-spreading hydrangea would not fit. Its slender panicles open greenish-white and age to a soft cream, held tightly along the upright stems rather than arching outward. Like other panicle hydrangeas it flowers on new wood and tolerates a hard cutback in late winter to maintain its narrow form.
sources: Chicago Botanic Garden Plant Evaluation Notes

planting.note: Plant in spring in a small-garden setting where its compact habit is an advantage.

directions: Dolly is a compact panicle hydrangea cultivar bearing small- to medium-sized conical white flower heads on a dense, well-branched shrub, making it a better fit for smaller gardens than the full-sized paniculata cultivars that can exceed eight feet. It flowers in mid- to late summer on new wood, so plants can be pruned back hard in late winter to maintain a tidy, compact habit. Culture is the same as other panicle hydrangeas: full sun, average well-drained soil, and consistent moisture during establishment.
sources: Chicago Botanic Garden Plant Evaluation Notes
